cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: I Can Handle This
cards.instruction: Perform complete emotional readiness while quietly borrowing coping strategies from every response around you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I'm completely prepared for this rejection email. Why have you brought water? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Small sips helped when I lost my job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. My approach exactly. Leave the jug; I prefer a thorough preparation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I had my sister read the email aloud. Want me to?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I always arrange a reader. Start gently; that's part of my system.

mechanism: A declares readiness to read rejection but borrows B water and delegated-reading strategies while exchanging practical roles to retain B support.
confusable: Unlike openly admitting inability to cope, A recasts B suggestions as the intended plan; borrowed authority modifies who does the reading and pouring.
comparison: One rejection recipient with a helper differs from peers waiting for two audition outcomes.
seedUse: D114-b sips and another person reading aloud; S02-a redefines the announced plan in response to B contribution.
